name: God of Prompt

sources.title: Homepage — commercial prompt library/AI products site (Robert Youssef); 20k+ customers, 100k+ subscribers claimed
Best AI Tools — editorially curated list of ~63 major tools ('the AI tools we actually use and recommend'); no submit form, partnerships email in footer

requirements: No public submission form — the 'Best AI Tools' list is hand-curated ('the AI tools we actually use and recommend')
Listings skew to established tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, n8n, Figma) paired with God of Prompt prompt resources
Only stated inbound channel: partnerships@ email shown in the site footer
preparation: A pitch to the partnerships email explaining the tool and why their prompt-library audience cares
Ideally a prompt resource angle — the list exists to drive prompt usage, so a tool that pairs well with their prompts/skills/MCP pages has the best fit
workflow: Email the partnerships contact (listed as [email protected] on the site footer) proposing inclusion in the Best AI Tools directory
Offer something useful to their audience (compatible prompts, a guide, affiliate/referral terms) — the site is commercially driven
If accepted, the tool appears on /best-ai-tools with an editorial description
watchFor: This is a commercial product site first — directory inclusion likely favors partners/affiliates, not free community submissions
The audience they claim (100k+ subscribers) is real reach, but the curated list is small (~63 tools) — acceptance odds are low
No SLA or stated review process for inbound pitches
countsAsLive: The product appears as a card on godofprompt.ai/best-ai-tools with an editorial write-up
unknowns: Whether inclusion is free, affiliate-based, or paid
Whether smaller/indie tools are ever accepted
